items.name: Readability
items.evidence: `get_fqdn` stores the punycoded value, then encodes it again on return: `return self._fqdn.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`. That redundancy is confusing. The wrapper shadows the stdlib name (`make_msgid as _make_msgid`) and copies the stdlib docstring in the 'Returns' style.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The inline `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` is copy-pasted 3 times (twice in utils.py, once in message.py), with no shared helper and no reuse in sanitize_address. The `make_msgid` wrapper is redundant once DNS_NAME is converted at the source. The test file's new import block is out of isort order.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Nothing hides failures with try/except. IDNA errors would surface instead of being swallowed, same as the reference. ASCII names pass through unchanged. `str(domain)` handles the lazy CachedDnsName object.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: The conversion happens at the source (`socket.getfqdn().encode('idna')`) and works for every encoding. ASCII hosts are unchanged and no errors are suppressed. But it repeats the idna call on every `get_fqdn` return and again in the `make_msgid` wrapper, so the same conversion is duplicated inline in several places.
